methodological_rigor.justification: Phase III RCT with primary endpoint ORR not met. Secondary endpoint OS analyzed without prespecified multiple testing correction. Stratified randomization and Cox regression appropriate. However, exploratory subgroup and sensitivity analyses without alpha adjustment reduce reliability. Post-hoc explorations of PPS, RFS not strengthened by prespecification.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: RCT (1b) in relevant population (RAS/BRAF wt mCRC). OS benefit modest (7.8-month improvement, HR 0.79, P=.049). Primary endpoint (ORR) negative; PFS, DOR non-significant. Clinical relevance tempered by lack of primary endpoint success and exploratory nature of OS finding.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT diagram provided. Methods describe treatment allocation, stratification. Safety and efficacy endpoints reported. However, open-label design limits blinding for efficacy (except possibly radiologist for ORR). No prespecified SAP publicly available at time of manuscript. Subgroup analyses not pre-registered.

novelty_literature.justification: First phase III RCT of mFOLFOXIRI+panitumumab vs mFOLFOX+panitumumab in RAS/BRAF wt mCRC. However, failed primary endpoint (ORR) and unplanned secondary OS analysis limit novelty. Incremental contribution to triplet chemotherapy landscape.

writing_presentation.justification: Adequately written with methods, results, discussion of subgroups. Kaplan-Meier curves included. Discussion appropriately contextualizes OS findings and acknowledges limitations of unplanned secondary analysis. Some complexity in interpreting multiple comparisons without clear alpha allocation.

key_strengths: Large sample (435 patients) and extended follow-up (60.2 months median) provide mature outcome data
OS benefit modest but statistically significant (HR 0.79, 7.8-month improvement) across subgroups
Comprehensive safety and efficacy reporting including ORR, PFS, post-progression survival
Stratified randomization by ECOG, tumor location, liver-only metastases reduces bias
key_concerns: Primary endpoint ORR not met (75% vs 78%, P=.442); lack of PFS benefit (HR 0.95) questions OS significance
OS is secondary endpoint analyzed without prespecified alpha correction for multiplicity
Unexplained discordance: OS benefit without ORR, DOR, PFS, or RFS differences suggests confounding or bias
Open-label design introduces potential investigator bias in treatment decisions after progression
Toxicity burden substantial (diarrhea 25% vs 8%, grade 3+ AE 62% vs 40%) may limit applicability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Failed primary endpoint with exploratory OS benefit detected in secondary analysis without multiplicity correction. Methodological rigor compromised. While OS finding intriguing, multiple discordances (ORR, PFS non-significant) warrant caution. Fits Tier 3; requires confirmation before practice adoption.
